messages:

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: Cost & model mix qualification for Acme Retail

Thanks again for taking time today — quick recap and a couple follow-ups on pricing/model mix so we can size a clean estimate.

Call recap (2/3 items):
- Primary use: in-product assistant for search + checkout help (chat), plus similarity search (embeddings) for recommendations and a light reranking layer for search results.
- Primary KPI: keep inference cost predictable while preserving critical chat quality for checkout flows.
- Next steps: we need token volumes (monthly) per feature, target budget ranges, and any target $/1M tokens you have in mind. Also confirm whether you expect most chat traffic to require high-quality chat model vs. a standard (quantized/open) chat model.

Can you confirm approximate monthly volumes for the three buckets below? A quick estimate is fine — we'll turn this into two pricing scenarios and a recommended model mix.
- Chat (assistant): _____ tokens/month
- Embeddings (similarity vectors): _____ tokens/month
- Rerank (query-level reordering): _____ tokens/month

I'll follow up with per-model unit economics and a short spreadsheet. I attached a draft estimate template (named Redwood_Estimate_ACME_20260302.pdf) that we'll populate once you share volumes.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0132

Subject: Re: Post-call: Cost & model mix qualification for Acme Retail

Marissa — thanks for the recap. Rough volumes based on our product roadmap & expected ramp:
- Chat (assistant): ~30,000,000 tokens/month
- Embeddings: ~5,000,000 tokens/month
- Rerank: ~3,000,000 tokens/month

Budget/context: we're targeting ~$3k/month to start (we can scale if unit economics justify it). Our public-facing checkout assistant needs higher quality on critical user flows (abandoned cart recovery, payment errors) but most routine queries could use a standard model.

Question: can Redwood present a per-model blended cost and a recommended split so we can see if we fit within ~$3k/mo? Also please call out how committed volume discounts or switching to a Dedicated pool would change the unit economics.

—Samir
Samir Desai, Head of Product | Acme Retail
samir@acme-retail.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Desai <samir@acme-retail.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Cost & model mix qualification for Acme Retail

Samir — great, thanks for the numbers and context. Below are two quick scenarios and a recommended model mix. I kept the math conservative; we can tighten numbers if you confirm exact traffic shape and tokenization assumptions.

Unit economics (list price examples per 1M tokens):
- High-quality chat (redwood-chat-1): $120 / 1M tokens
- Standard chat (open-chat-quant): $12 / 1M tokens
- Embeddings (embed-1): $6 / 1M tokens
- Rerank (rerank-1): $20 / 1M tokens

Your volumes: chat 30M, embeddings 5M, rerank 3M. Two scenarios:
1) Quality-first (mix: 60% high-quality chat, 40% standard)
   - Chat: 30M tokens = (18M HQ * $120 + 12M Std * $12) = $2,160 + $144 = $2,304
   - Embeddings: 5M * $6 = $30
   - Rerank: 3M * $20 = $60
   - Total = $2,394 / month

2) Cost-first (mix: 100% standard chat)
   - Chat: 30M * $12 = $360
   - Embeddings: 5M * $6 = $30
   - Rerank: 3M * $20 = $60
   - Total = $450 / month

Observation: your $3k/mo target is feasible under the quality-first scenario and easily met under the cost-first scenario. The big lever is % of traffic we route to the high-quality chat model.

Recommendations / next steps:
- Suggested model mix to start: 30% HQ chat for checkout-critical flows (e.g., payment/checkout contexts) and 70% standard chat for routine assistant queries. That gives a middle-ground cost of ~ (9M HQ, 21M Std) => $1,188 + $252 + $30 + $60 = ~$1,530/mo.
- Offer: I'll include two purchase options in the attached estimate: \"Pay-as-you-go (hosted)\" and \"12-mo committed (Dedicated)\" with step discounts at 100M and 500M committed tokens that reduce HQ cost by ~30% and Std by ~15%.
- POC: propose 2-week pilot using a production-like traffic sample so we can measure tokenization, actual prefix lengths, and effective costs. We'll instrument per-route latency and cost.

Attached: Redwood_Estimate_ACME_20260302.pdf (line-item estimates + committed discount tiers). I'll draft a simple SOW for the pilot and a 12-mo committed option (attached separate SOW draft).

Proposed quick sync: Thu 3/4 10:00am PT to walk the estimate and decisions. Does that work?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0132
[Attachment: Redwood_Estimate_ACME_20260302.pdf (PDF, 120KB); Attachment: SOW_draft_ACME_20260302.docx (DOCX, 45KB)]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 18:00:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Pricing note / recommended ask

Marissa / Lauren — quick internal note while the estimate is fresh:
- If they want to target $3k/mo, aim the proposal at the quality-first scenario but with a staged rollout: start with 30% HQ (checkout) + 70% Std; that lands around $1.5k/mo so we can offer a modest discount and still present a path to $3k if they increase HQ traffic.
- Discount strategy: propose a 12-mo committed agreement (ACME-2026-01) with a 10% discount at 100M tokens and 25% at 300M. That preserves room for margin and upsell.
- Pilot SOW: include explicit acceptance metrics (cost-per-1M verification, 95th pct latency on checkout flows), and an option to convert pilot consumption into committed credits to avoid double-billing.

I'll attach the SOW draft I started in the thread. If you want, I can join Thu's sync to walk technical SLAs and Dedicated options.

—Connor
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOW_draft_ACME_20260302.docx (DOCX, 45KB)]
